projects.name: 2.1.2.14 - Strengthen the national health care and nutrition systems
projects.description:
1) In 2023,  strategic partnership with Azerbaijan Food Safety Agency was strenghtened by initiation of dialogue on several projects, including  FEEDCities. By the end of the year, three meetings on  the scope of the FEEDCities in Azerbaijan, area of implementation and contractual  details were held. The objectives of the FEEDCities research are:
1. To describe the characteristics of the food being sold at street vending places, map their location, characterize the street food offer at selected vending places and describe the costumers present and the street foods purchased.
2. To assess the nutritional composition of the ready-to-eat foods sold in the street.
3. To map the spatial distribution of food advertisements and to describe the typology and contents of food advertisements.   
2) Expert team composed of WHO national and international experts, as well as representatives from Republican Hygiene and Epidemiology Center (HEC) visited selected Hygiene and Epidemiology Centers (HEC) in Sabunchu, Sabail, Ganja, Masalli, Astara districts, . The visits aimed to assess institutional capacities of these HECs in delivering essential public health functions and to identify the structural and functional refinements needed for better contribution to public health in Azerbaijan.
 During the visit experts conducted unstructured interviews with directors of HECs and public health workers, The information collected was used to produce a report with key recommendations for reform to the Ministry of Health. 
3)The World Health Organization (WHO) organized a meeting in Azerbaijan, with representatives from key health agencies to create a shared understanding of strengthening the country's public health system. Participants represented MoH, SAMHI, TABİB, the Food Safety Agency, The State Customs Committee, Public Health and Reforms Center, Azerbaijan Medical University, Ministry of Emergency Situations, and the Azerbaijan State Advanced Training Institute for Doctors. During the meeting, participants identified their institution’s role in delivering essential public health services and agreed on the need for having a platform to strengthen collaboration in addressing main public health challenges. 
Participants agreed to expand the group to include the Ministry of Ecology, Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, State Committee for Family, Women and Children and Health Committee of the Parliament. The idea of a Public Health Symposium, involving national and international partners, was explored to raise awareness and discuss global health trends, fostering enhanced cooperation.

projects.name: 3.1.1.10 - Enabling FLW prevention and reduction to promote GHG emissions mitigation and food security
projects.description: The connection between FLW and climate change lies in the significant amount of GHG emissions produced throughout the food supply chain, from production and distribution to consumption and disposal. When food goes to waste, all the resources used in its production such as water, energy and land are also wasted along with the emissions generated. GHGs contribute to an unstable climate prone to drastic environmental change and extreme weather events. These unstable climate conditions negatively impact crop yields, reduce the nutritional quality of crops, disrupt supply chains, and threaten food security. Halving FLW would help Azerbaijan realize its NDC commitments and meet Target 12.3 of the SDGs, which calls to cut FLW in half by 2030, as well as improve food security and nutrition and ease pressure on natural resources. Prevention and reduction of FLW contributes to climate change mitigation, increases food availability, and minimizes economic losses for affected food supply chain actors. FLW lowers productivity and that is transmitted through food prices. Therefore, prevention and reduction of food losses have downstream and upstream impacts. Particular attention should be paid to the fact that economic decisions underlie much of FLW and that measurement needs to improve and should account for both quantity and quality losses. Leveraging social and technological innovation for food and agriculture – focused on FLW prevention and reduction – is of paramount importance to scale up solutions that can drive systemic changes. FLW and climate change affect diversity of diets and food production that rely on biodiversity which is crucial for combating food insecurity and malnutrition and ensuring food systems resilience.

projects.name: 2.1.3.19 - Empowering and Increasing Resilience of Civil Society Organizations to Assist GBV and TIP Survivors In Azerbaijan
projects.description:
Gender-based violence (GBV) is often cited as a major push factor to trafficking in persons (TIP).In Azerbaijan, survivors of GBV and TIP are closely interlinked in terms of the provision of protection by civil society organizations (CSOs). According to the International Men & Gender Equality Survey (IMAGES), about 32% of women in Azerbaijan report having been abused by their spouses at some point in their lifetime, and according to the GRETA report, a total of 472 survivors of TIP were formally identified in Azerbaijan, between 2018 and 2022, of whom 94% were women.
Despite progress made in eliminating GBV and TIP in Azerbaijan, challenges remain, including providing full protection and ensuring the successful reintegration of survivors. These challenges are largely related to a lack of capacities and resources on the side of service providers, namely CSOs. Legal and bureaucratic barriers introduced through legislative changes made in 2014 limit access of CSOs to funding from international donors considerably. At the same time, the level of government funding for some of these organizations has not increased significantly to match the shortfalls. The uncertainty regarding the changes in the national legislation in favour of CSOs and the lack of a sustainable budget for them has led service providers to face difficulties in providing protection and reintegration options for potential, presumed and confirmed victims of GBV and TIP.
This project aims to empower and strengthen the resilience of CSOs in Azerbaijan to enable them to provide quality, timely and gender-sensitive services to persons vulnerable to GBV and TIP and survivors of GBV and TIP, irrespective of gender, age, disabilities and legal status and protect them from violence, exploitation and abuse. This will be done by strengthening partnerships and coordination across Government and non-government agencies and increasing the capacities and resources of CSOs in Azerbaijan.

projects.name: 3.1.2.4 Promoting Kahriz Rehabilitation for Enhanced Water-Related Climate Adaptation in Azerbaijan
projects.description: Funded by IOM Sasakawa Endowment Fund. The Kahriz is a traditional decentralized water supply system in Azerbaijan, which is fed through subterranean water. It has played a vital role in accessing groundwater extraction since ancient times in the arid zones of Azerbaijan. It is estimated that at least 1,400 Kahrizes exist in 20 regions of Azerbaijan. There is a growing recognition of Kahrizes as a nature-based solution and of the importance of rehabilitating them as an eco-friendly method for water extraction, especially in the face of climate change and water scarcity. In light of the above, the objective of this project is to contribute to enhanced water-related adaptation in the context of long-term impacts of climate variability and change in the Republic of Azerbaijan. The project will support government entities and project stakeholders to promote Kahriz rehabilitation as a climate change adaptation measure (Outcome 1) by making available evidence-based data and analysis promoting the rehabilitation of Kahrizes (Output 1.1) and by increasing the awareness and understanding of national stakeholders on the benefits of the Kahriz as a climate change adaptation measure, and equipping them to mobilize private investment (Output 1.2).

projects.name: 2.1.2.3 - Strengthen primary health care and comprehensive essential health services
projects.description:
1) WHO Azerbaijan Country Office held the first seminar of the long-term action plan for supporting the adaptation of competencies of public health workers in Azerbaijan to international standards in the field. To assess the knowledge and skill competencies of the public health workforce in the country members of the "Public Health Capacity Group", staff of the Faculty of Public Health of Azerbaijan Medical University, and WHO experts attended the seminar. During the workshop, the participants were introduced to the "Competency Framework" model set by the WHO – ASPHER, in which they discussed and evaluated their own competencies. Moving forward, the plan was to prepare evidence-based recommendations on changes in medical education curricula to help Azerbaijan's public health professionals to develop competencies defined by international standards. The action is funded by USAID and implemented by WHO in collaboration with the Ministry of Health, the State Agency for Mandatory Health Insurance and TABIB.

2) WHO Azerbaijan hosted a workshop with experts from health education and health provider institutions, to develop small-scale COPC intervention plans in Nasimi district. The goal was to improve health outcomes in the District via collaboration between healthcare providers and the community while considering population characteristics and prioritizing health problems. On the first day, participants visited the District's health centers to observe and collect data on the population’s health and identify common health issues. For the remaining days, they worked on community characterization, prioritization of health issues, and a detailed assessment of health problems. The working groups then developed a comprehensive COPC intervention plans for the District. This workshop was organized under the public health focus areas of the APR funded by USAID and implemented by WHO in collaboration with the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Azerbaijan, the SAMHI, TABIB, and supported by Nasimi District Executive Power of Baku.

3) In this seminar, the participants  studied the "Public Health Competency Framework" developed by the WHO–ASPHER and self-assessed their competencies. The seminar was attended by members of the "Capacity Group on Public Health" representing MoH, TABIB and SAMHI, teachers of the Faculty of Public Health of Azerbaijan Medical University, and WHO experts. Discussions were held on the individual learning plans presented at the seminar and the gaps between international standards and local competencies identified in the evaluations. The outcome of the seminar is that Participants have become familiar with the ASPHER competency framework, which identified their learning needs and developed time-bound individual learning plans with the support of WHO experts. The long-term aim is to prepare evidence-based recommendations on changes in medical education curricula to help Azerbaijan's public health professionals develop competencies defined by international standards.

4) Zaur Aliyev, Chairman of the Board of the State Agency for Mandatory Health Insurance, Vugar Gurbanov, Executive Director of the Management Union of Medical Territorial Units (TABIB), and Dr. Hande Harmancı, World Health Organization (WHO) Representative in Azerbaijan, visited the Shamakhi district to assess the efforts undertaken by the WHO Country Office in Shamakhi to strengthen primary health care (PHC) services. The purpose of the visit was to familiarize themselves with the work carried out until now and discuss future collaborations between WHO and the country's health institutions in this field. 

WHO Azerbaijan has so far implemented the PHC Demonstration, Shamakhi Fellowship Program, and other PHC-related activities in the district to develop an accessible, quality, and comprehensive primary health care model, improve the knowledge and skills of local medical workers, and strengthen the medical staff's capacity for PHC. 

5) Agencies responsible for planning and delivering public health services in Azerbaijan, online meeting brought together again representatives from  Ministry of Health, SAMHI, TABİB, Food Safety Agency of The Republic of Azerbaijan, The State Customs Committee of the Republic of Azerbaijan, Public Health and Rgeforms Center, Azerbaijan Medical University,, Ministry of Emergency Situations and Azerbaijan State Advanced Training Institute for Doctors, the Ministry of Ecology, Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, State Committee for Family, Women and Children as well as the Health Committee of the Parliament. The session aimed to create a shared understanding of the need to renew the public health system in Azerbaijan and the role that each institution can play. A notable outcome was the formation of a collaborative working group dedicated to strengthening Azerbaijan's public health policy framework and underscored a collective commitment to advancing the nation's public health landscape.

projects.name: 2.1.2.32 - Support to enhance national capacity on vaccination
projects.description:
1) To support Azerbaijan’s government efforts on ensuring the successful uptake of routine childhood vaccination, series of training for HCWs were organized in four regions of Azerbaijan (Goygol, Yevlakh, Minghechevir, Gobustan) that are the regions with lowest vaccination among under 6 years old children together with UNICEF and in collaboration with MoH, TABIB, SAMHI, and regional executive power offices. The main goal of the training was to enhance the skills of healthcare workers in those regions based on best practice guidelines for routine immunization.  During the event, 136 PHC workers were trained.
Stakeholders: MoH, TABIB, SAMHI, UNICEF

2) The interactive events aimed to build trust and demand for vaccines among parents, by providing them with accurate information about vaccines and dispelling myths and misconceptions about their safety and efficacy. 

As part of the campaign, 500 families with children who missed their routine immunizations have been personally invited to the meeting with trusted health-care professionals. In a single day of activities, about 70% of the un- and under-immunized children received their vaccines while nearly 80% of attending parents had initially delayed or declined vaccination of these children. 
Stakeholders: MoH, TABIB, SAMHI, UNICEF
Beneficieries: population, parents

3) WHO, the Azerbaijan Pediatric Society (AzPC), and TABIB conducted trainings on October 27 and November 17 in Shirvan and Lankaran cities, respectively. 
This event was dedicated to underscoring the significance of child vaccination. A series of events organized in the regions, titled "Embracing Scientific Evidence Over Myths: Vaccination Awareness Training," was held under the motto "Leave no one behind" in accordance with the WHO's European Immunization Agenda 2030. The primary goal of the training was to enhance the skills of healthcare workers in those regions based on best practice guidelines for routine immunization. 
The event involved 132 pediatricians and nurses from Shirvan and 76 healthcare workers from Lankaran and surrounding cities.
Stakeholders: MoH, TABIB, AzPc 

4) To raise awareness on vaccination, WHO, the Azerbaijan Pediatric Society (AzPC), and TABIB conducted awareness-raising events on October 27 and November 17 in Shirvan and Lankaran cities, respectively. During the events, Board Members of AzPC and experts from the Ministry of Health engaged in discussions with parents on vaccine hesitancy and addressed their queries. The primary goal of the meetings was to enhance parents' awareness regarding vaccination while dispelling misconceptions about vaccines. The two events involved 73 parents who had initially refused vaccination.

5) To support Azerbaijan’s government in promoting routine childhood vaccination, various educational materials were developed:
1. Questions & Answers Brochure: Addresses key questions and dispels vaccine myths. Printed and distributed during European Immunization Week and other vaccine-related events, with 197,750 copies.
2. Brochure on Vaccine-Preventable Diseases: Provides fundamental vaccine information. 7,750 copies delivered, more to be distributed after approval of the new national immunization calendar.
3. Measles Poster and Flyer: 5,300 posters distributed to vaccine facilities via TABIB at immunization events. Additionally, 203,000 flyers printed and are being distributed during awareness events.
4. Rubella Poster and Flyer: 5,300 posters distributed via TABIB at immunization events. Furthermore, 203,000 flyers printed and are being disseminated during events.
5. Vaccine Puzzle: Entertaining and educational material for kids. 600 pieces printed and disseminated to  caregivers during awareness-raising events.

Aim: to provide evidence-based information, to raise awareness
Stakeholders: MoH, TABIB, SAMHI
Main beneficaries: Caregivers, vaccine-hesitant families.

projects.name: 2.1.2.7 - Strengthen longer-term planning for and capacity building of health care workers.
projects.description:
1) Pandemic Fund Meeting
WHO Azerbaijan developed the joint proposal, “Pandemic Fund Participatory OneHealth Disease Detection in Azerbaijan (PF-AZE-PODD)” for funding to address the ongoing challenges presented by pandemic threats. PF-AZE-PODD project aimed to establish a community level early warning system through One Health approach by creating teams of “One Health Workers”, supported by digital platform for early detection and alarm verification with integration into existing national surveillance system for strengthened identification and response to unexpected human and animal health events leading to improved prevention of epidemics and pandemics.
 Developed proposal was presented and discussed with senior government officials from MoH, TABIB, SAMHI, MoF, Heydar Aliyev Foundation, Agrarian Services Agency and Azerbaijan Food Safety Agency to align it with National Priorities and Investment plans. Proposal components and application process were introduced and discussed. The key points were discussed during final Ministerial Sessions and proposal was approved by the Minister of Health. 

2) A delegation from WHO Azerbaijan has started an official visit to Nakhchivan

During this meeting, extensive discussions were held on various topics, including primary health care, emergency medicine, laboratory services, public health, and medical education. 

The WHO Azerbaijan team has started a 3-day visit to Nakhchivan, led by Dr. Hande Harmanci, WHO Representative to Azerbaijan, in response to an invitation from the Ministry of Health of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic.

As part of the visit's framework, the WHO delegation is expected to become familiar with with the healthcare system reforms implemented in the Autonomous Republic in recent months, the efforts aimed at enhancing the quality of medical services, and the projects planned for the near future. In addition to visiting Nakhchivan city, they will also visit the Ordubad and Sharur regions, where they will inspect the newly established Family Health Care Centers.

3) The two-day workshop brought together experts from the Ministry of Health, Republic Hygiene and Epidemiology Center, Regional Hygiene and Epidemiology Centers, Public Health and Reforms Center, and WHO. The goal was to raise awareness on the need for transforming the public health system to address the health challenges affecting people living in Azerbaijan. Using the framework of the essential public health functions, participants engaged in discussions to identify main strengths, weaknesses, threats and opportunities. The information collected was used to inform the development of a report with key recommendations for reform to the Ministry of Health. The methodology for engagement used in he workshop also supported strengthening collaboration between the participants, with a view to strengthen public health in Azerbaijan

4) In collaboration with faculty members from Azerbaijan Medical University (AMU) Public Health Faculty and Medical Education Department, and ASATID, a survey was planned to assess the public health competencies of senior medical students of the Public Health Faculty using the WHO-ASPHER competency framework.    In addition, the same survey was adapted for faculty members so that the programme could evaluate the extent to which these competencies were gained in the program, and they were also asked to answer. 94 medical students and 30 faculty member participated in the study. The mean scores across categories in ASPHER competencies reveal strengths and areas for improvement. The findings of the survey were presented at a Public Health Congress in Turkey. The survey will continue on residents and public health practitioners. This result of the study will facilitate the identify learning needs, inform curriculum development process, and contribute to public health education strengthening in Azerbaijan.

5) WHO Azerbaijan Country Office held the first seminar of the long-term action plan for supporting the adaptation of competencies of public health workers in Azerbaijan to international standards in the field. To assess the knowledge and skill competencies of the public health workforce in the country members of the "Public Health Capacity Group", staff of the Faculty of Public Health of Azerbaijan Medical University, and WHO experts attended the seminar. During the workshop, the participants were introduced to the "Competency Framework" model set by the WHO – ASPHER, in which they discussed and evaluated their own competencies. Moving forward, the plan was to prepare evidence-based recommendations on changes in medical education curricula to help Azerbaijan's public health professionals to develop competencies defined by international standards. The action is funded by USAID and implemented by WHO in collaboration with the Ministry of Health, the State Agency for Mandatory Health Insurance and TABIB.

projects.name: 2.1.2.25 - Support the country for better protection of its people by preparedness to rapidly detect and respond to health emergencies
projects.description:
1) WHO Azerbaijan CO held a community engagement event to promote and raise awareness of the importance of learning cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) skills among the public at different locations in Baku. CPR is a vital first response during sudden cardiac arrest. It is not necessary to be a medical professional to perform CPR and anyone can learn these skills. A total of 310 participants had a chance to learn and apply CPR on the special mannequin under the supervision of our doctors during the event. 

2) The WHO Country Office in Azerbaijan, in collaboration with the Ministry of Health, SAMHI, and TABIB, is implementing the Azerbaijan Pandemic Response (APR) Activity. Focusing on the Emergency Care Systems, a brochure was designed to inform the public about the importance of learning the correct technique of cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) skills. The design included instructional photos to implement CPR, text information, and a QR link directing to the instruction video. The brochures were shared with participants at our 28 Mall community engagement and WHO's 75th-anniversary events.

3) As part of the World Health Organization (WHO) Emergencies Program and the EU-funded 'Vaccination Support' project, WHO Azerbaijan, in collaboration with the WHO Regional Office for Europe, organized a workshop on 'Infodemic Management.' The aim of this workshop was to support the fight against the infodemic and contribute to a healthier information ecosystem. The event brought together about 30 journalists, social media influencers, and representatives from local health agencies to enhance their skills in identifying and combatting misinformation and disinformation related to vaccination, especially concerning their impact on public health.
During the workshop, participants received briefings on various topics, including risk communication and community engagement, the media's role in health emergencies, routine immunization, the concept of the infodemic, and its management.  The presentations covered subjects such as detecting infodemic risks and responding to infodemic signals through social listening.
